sources.quote: good INP is 200 milliseconds or less. INP replaced First Input Delay in March 2024
sources.title: Interaction to Next Paint is officially a Core Web Vital 🚀 | Blog | web.dev
sources.evidence: As of March 12, 2024, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) is officially a Core Web Vital metric, replacing First Input Delay. Pages should have an INP of 200 milliseconds or less to provide a good user experience. Support for FID ended on September 9, 2024.

sources.quote: private and non profit organizations with 50 or more employees in Ontario must meet WCAG 2.0 Level AA on public facing web content, excluding live captions and pre recorded audio description
sources.title: How to make websites accessible | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: For Business/Non-Profit organizations with 50 or more employees, all public websites and web content posted after January 1, 2012 must meet WCAG 2.0, Level A and AA other than live captions and pre-recorded audio descriptions. Organizations with fewer than 50 employees are not required to follow these website accessibility requirements, but are encouraged to do so.

sources.quote: Organizations with 20 or more employees also file an accessibility compliance report, next due 31 December 2026
sources.title: Completing your accessibility compliance report | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: For businesses or non-profit organizations with 20 or more employees, the reporting deadline is December 31, 2026. These organizations must file an accessibility compliance report every three years.

sources.quote: They reference Canada's adopted version of EN 301 549, which incorporates WCAG 2.1 Level AA, on an ambulatory basis
sources.title: Canada Gazette, Part 2, Volume 159, Number 26: Regulations Amending the Accessible Canada Regulations
sources.evidence: The amendments incorporate by reference the most recent version of the CAN/ASC - EN 301 549 without modification on an ambulatory basis. The EN 301 549 standard includes WCAG 2.1 level A and AA.

sources.quote: Obligations phase in across 5 December 2027 and 5 December 2028, and bind federally regulated entities such as banks and telecoms
sources.title: Guidance overview of regulatory amendments: Digital Technologies Phase 1 - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: The requirements of the amended Regulations will come into force on December 5, 2027, and December 5, 2028. The Phase 1 Regulations apply to federal public sector organizations and federally regulated private sector organizations.

sources.quote: The same date dropped the francisation registration threshold at the Office québécois de la langue française from 50 employees to 25
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française
sources.title: Démarche de francisation : Les entreprises employant de 25 à 49 personnes sont invitées à s’inscrire à l’Office québécois de la langue française sans attendre
sources.evidence: As of June 1, 2025, the obligation to register with the Office québécois de la langue française to undertake a francization process extends to businesses with 25 to 49 employees, including those under federal jurisdiction.

sources.quote: CIRA sets the wholesale price of a.CA at $10.50
sources.title: How much does a .CA domain cost? - CIRA
sources.evidence: The wholesale price for a .CA domain is $10.50 CAD, as set by the registry. All .CA Certified Registrars are billed at the same wholesale cost; different registrars set different retail prices.

sources.quote: Under section 13(4) of the Copyright Act an assignment of copyright is valid only in writing and signed
sources.title: Copyright Act ( RSC , 1985, c. C-42) - Justice Laws Website
sources.evidence: Section 13(4): no assignment or grant is valid unless it is in writing signed by the owner of the right in respect of which the assignment or grant is made, or by the owner's duly authorized agent. Section 13(1): the author of a work shall be the first owner of the copyright therein.

flags.quote: That deadline was 1 January 2025 and has passed
flags.issue: The AODA deadline for organizations with 50 or more employees to make public websites and web content conform to WCAG 2.0 Level AA was January 1, 2021, not January 1, 2025. Ontario's guidance states the requirement applies to web content posted after January 1, 2012 and became effective as of January 1, 2021.
